"""Starting architecture: the main campaign's default policy (conv encoder, width 64, depth 2, ReLU,
no normalisation), rewritten as a candidate file. A 3x3 conv body, a 1x1 conv placement head
(one logit per brick type and anchor cell), and DONE and value heads on mean+max pooled features."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. The baseline is very noisy: its 4 seeds scored 0.068, 0.068, 0.258 and 0.068, so one seed in four found a much better solution. With the default recipe, 131k steps at 4,096 steps per update gives only 32 PPO updates. With a linearly decaying learning rate, that is probably too few for a policy over about 400 actions to settle reliably. My best guess is that the main bottleneck is the number of optimisation steps and samples, not how much each sample is reused. A second guess is that gamma 0.95 discounts the +1 exact-build bonus too heavily: over 20 placements it shrinks to about 0.36, so the agent cares too little about finishing exactly. An entropy bonus of 0.01 may also keep the policy too random. This round tests three directions separately: more updates, more samples with fewer epochs, and longer-horizon credit with less entropy.
analyses.2: All three round-1 recipes scored 0.068 on every seed, which is 35 of 512 designs. That matches the baseline's usual result (three of its four seeds). So 0.068 looks like a sticky local optimum. The one baseline seed that reached 0.258 got there by luck, not by recipe. None of the changes so far let a run escape: halving the batch for twice as many updates, using about 1.8 times more samples with 2 epochs, or a longer horizon with lower entropy. Train success at the end (0.054–0.064) is also flat, so each policy is stuck rather than overfitting. Two levers are still untested: a much larger step size, and more exploration (higher entropy). A further option is the extreme 'many fresh samples' setting (1 epoch, about 426k steps) with a stronger learning rate. Every run takes about 40 s, so time limits are not a concern.
analyses.3: At lr 0.001, every recipe sat on the 0.068 plateau, which looks like a degenerate policy: smaller batches, more samples, 1 or 2 epochs and a longer horizon all scored about 0.068. Only changes that make the policy move further escaped it. lr 0.003 scored 0.378 (seeds 0.27 and 0.49), clearly above the baseline mean of 0.116 even with the seed noise. ent_coef 0.03 scored 0.20, but one of its two seeds was still stuck at 0.068. So the bottleneck seems to be how far each update moves the policy and how well it keeps exploring, not the number of samples. Training takes about 40 s, far under the time limit. This round keeps lr 0.003 and tests one more change on top of it in each candidate: more entropy, more gradient steps per update, and longer-horizon credit assignment. The last two rounds can then combine whatever helps.
analyses.4: At lr 0.001, every run stayed on the 0.068 plateau, whatever the batch size, epochs, horizon or entropy. Raising lr to 0.003 escaped it (0.378). Using 64 minibatches on top of that, for twice the gradient steps, gave the best result so far: 0.515, with both seeds high (0.56 and 0.47). So the main bottleneck seems to be how far the policy moves during the short budget. Adding high entropy (0.03) to lr 0.003 did not help (0.365, within noise). A long horizon (gamma 0.99) hurt badly (0.106), so the default gamma of 0.95 should stay. lr is now at its upper bound and minibatches are at their 64-sample minimum. The remaining ways to move the policy further are a wider clip range, more updates from smaller batches, and lower entropy so the greedy policy sharpens. Each candidate makes one change to r3c2. This is the last round, so the 4-seed re-runs will decide.
